- [X] I am using the latest released version of Numba (most recent is visible in
 the change log (https://github.com/numba/numba/blob/master/CHANGE_LOG).
- [X] I have included below a minimal working reproducer (if you are unsure how
 to write one see http://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports).

The documentation of what `bind()` says it will do and what the implementation does don't seem to match (or if they do, the documentation is pretty ambiguous) - in https://github.com/numba/numba/blob/master/numba/cuda/cudadrv/devicearray.py#L135-L141

```python
def bind(self, stream=0):
    """Bind a CUDA stream to this object so that all subsequent operation
    on this array defaults to the given stream.
    """
    clone = copy.copy(self)
    clone.stream = stream
    return clone
```

Using a modified reproducer from the now-closed #2664:

```python
from numba import cuda
import numpy as np
stream = cuda.stream()
with stream.auto_synchronize():
    arr = cuda.device_array(
        (3, 3), 
        dtype=np.float64)
    arr.bind(stream)
    assert arr.stream == stream
```

results in:

```
$ python repro.py 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 9, in <module>
    assert arr.stream == stream
AssertionError
```
title: DeviceNDArray.bind() does not seem to bind the stream to self
